title: Focal control of thalamocortical gain shapes perception.
abstract: The convergence of sensory and modulatory inputs in layer 4 of primary sensory cortex establishes a point of control with powerful potential: what passes through this gate determines, for all downstream circuits, what exists in the world. Modulatory control of layer 4 thalamocortical synapses should thus be profoundly impactful. We used nicotine to modify processing at thalamocortical synapses in macaque primary visual cortex, while recording across the full cortical depth; the resulting focal gain change altered neural responses across all layers of cortex. The circuit did not compensate for these changes, and so they propagated to bias perceived stimulus contrast. That modulation applied to a tiny volume of tissue at the gate to cortex-via one receptor type, for one modulator-reshapes population coding and alters perception, implies that an organismal-level accounting of neuromodulatory control of cognition, emotion and behavior must reckon with the profound capacity for neuromodulatory modification of sensation.
